findings.reason: the two directories item 3 removes (`~/.cache/nova/jax-compilation`, `~/.cache/nova/kernels`) are exactly the ones the named routes own, and a benchmark pointed at an arbitrary path sits outside §5's stated "gate jobs" aim, so the overbroad sentence does not send a builder's fix to the wrong code path.
findings.text: §5 asserts "Every nova route that enables the persistent cache also disables XLA's per-fusion autotune cache", but its own enumeration names only three routes, and several nova modules enable the persistent cache by calling `jax.config.update("jax_compilation_cache_dir", ...)` directly (e.g. `benchmarks/receipt_raster_check.py:129`, `benchmarks/receipt_topology_check.py:97`, `benchmarks/solve_compile_cadence.py:161`), which bypass both named functions and receive the export only when launched through the lane or pre-warm

response_events.reason: Benchmarks that set jax_compilation_cache_dir directly are not gate jobs and write to roots outside the inventory. The node's done-when lists the routes it covers, and the lane and pre-warm exports still reach those benchmarks whenever they run there.

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when names its negative control explicitly ("removing either export fails its test, which is the negative control"), and each of its three clauses (export tests, runtime-identity test, titan zero-file run with a second-run cache hit) is measurable against a named artifact.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — evidence lands in the tracked `docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html`, and the arms use fresh cache roots under node-local `/tmp` as scratch only, never as the record.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s5 introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into symbols, filenames or comments; the only new names are JAX's own environment variables and a mechanism-named research file.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold: the stated root cause (autotune file creates in flight during teardown, matching the still-present 0-byte tmp files and the 09:39:25→09:40:32 window) is the one the cited evidence shows; the mechanism (setting `jax_persistent_cache_enable_xla_caches` to `none` before the identity is computed, plus the env export on the lane and pre-warm) is capable of producing the zero-file done-when; and its callers are named (`configure_persistent_compilation_cache`, `tiledassembly.compilation_cache`, the lane prelude, `prewarm.sh`). One sentence is broader than the evidence given — see the finding.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — every work item (disable the per-fusion cache on each route, the four-arm titan comparison, the cache inventory and removal) serves the one goal of removing autotune writes to GPFS.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's `data-links` to `s4` resolves, and the §4-after-§5 ordering is stated in the "Order with §4" paragraph (line 424) rather than only implied, answering the mutual-write hazard an earlier review raised.
